# Balance the Data and the Context

## Data ink and non-data ink

- Data elements: points, bars, shaded areas
- Context elements: axes, ticks, labels, legends, annotations, grids
- Tufte: "Maximize the data-ink ratio, *within reason*"
- The qualifier is the point: remove clutter, but do not strip context

## Too much non-data ink

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Body fat vs. height of male Australian athletes
- Frames around the figure, panel, and legend
- A heavy grid pulls attention from the data

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-grid-bad", fig_aus_athletes_grid_bad(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Cleaned up

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Frames removed, minor grid lines removed
- Major grid lines in light gray, behind the data
- Open grid with no axis lines signals that values could extend beyond the shown range

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-grid-good", fig_aus_athletes_grid_good(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Too little non-data ink

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Faint axis labels and titles are hard to see
- Points seem to float in space
- The legend is not set apart from the data

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-aus-athletes-min-bad", fig_aus_athletes_min_bad(),
          w = 5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Small multiples need structure

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Without facet frames or a baseline, bars seem to float
- It is hard to tell which part belongs to which facet
- Fix: a gray panel background per facet and thin horizontal grid lines

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-titanic-facets-bad", fig_titanic_facets_bad(),
          w = 4, h = 5, x = 9.5, y = 1.4, width = 5.5)
```

## Background grids: the ggplot2 default

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- White grid on gray background: one visual unit, but a prominent grid
- Here the grid overpowers the data lines

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-price-plot-ggplot-default", fig_price_plot_ggplot_default(),
          w = 5, h = 3.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## No grid, no anchor

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Without any grid, the lines are not anchored
- We cannot tell how far they end above or below the index value of 100

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-price-plot-no-grid", fig_price_plot_no_grid(),
          w = 5, h = 3.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Add a reference line

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- At minimum, one thin line at the index value of 100
- It gives context for the whole time span

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-price-plot-refline", fig_price_plot_refline(),
          w = 5, h = 3.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Or a minimal grid

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Thin horizontal lines at the major y ticks
- Draw lines orthogonal to the direction in which the numbers vary
- No prominent axis lines are needed
- For horizontal bars, use vertical grid lines

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-price-plot-hgrid", fig_price_plot_hgrid(),
          w = 5, h = 3.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Paired data: draw the diagonal

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Gene expression in mutant vs. wild-type bacteriophage T7
- The relevant reference is x = y, not a grid
- Genes above or below the line are higher or lower in the mutant

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-gene-expression-diagonal", fig_gene_expression_diagonal(),
          w = 4.2, h = 4.2, x = 9, y = 1.6, width = 6.3)
```

## Paired data: a grid obscures the point

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A background grid hides which genes are above or below x = y
- Adding the diagonal on top of the grid makes the figure too busy

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-gene-expression-grid", fig_gene_expression_grid(),
          w = 4.2, h = 4.2, x = 9, y = 1.6, width = 6.3)
```

## Summary

- Both too much and too little non-data ink hurt
- Data should be the main emphasis, with enough context to read it
- Be judicious with grid lines: show only the ones most informative for this plot
- Light, minimal grids on white are a good default
